hook: The Corsican officer who crowned himself emperor and conquered most of Europe.

pages.x: Napoleon Bonaparte was born in 1769 in Ajaccio, on Corsica, a year after France took the island. At nine he was sent to a military school in France, where the other boys mocked his accent. At 16 he became an artillery officer.

In 1793, during the French Revolution, the British held the port of Toulon. The young captain worked out where to put the guns to drive their fleet from the harbour. It worked, and at 24 he was made a general.
In 1796 he led a ragged army into Italy and beat the Austrians again and again. In 1798 he invaded Egypt and beat the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids, though the British sank his fleet.

He took 167 scholars to Egypt to study the country. In 1799 his soldiers dug up a stone carved with the same text in Greek and in hieroglyphs. Thanks to it, the scholar Champollion learned to read hieroglyphs in 1822.
Back in France he seized power in 1799. In 1804, in Notre-Dame in Paris, with the pope looking on, he took the crown and placed it on his own head: Napoleon I, Emperor of the French.
His code of laws, of 1804, made all men equal before the law, ended the old privileges of the nobles and protected property. It is still the basis of the law in France and in many countries.
In 1805 he crushed the armies of the Austrian and Russian emperors at Austerlitz, his greatest victory. By 1810 he ruled or controlled most of Europe, and put his brothers on its thrones.
In 1812 he invaded Russia with some 600,000 men. He reached Moscow, but the Russians set it on fire. His army retreated through the winter, starving and freezing, and most of them never came back.

Beaten by all of Europe, he was exiled in 1814 to the little island of Elba. Within a year he escaped and returned to Paris. For a hundred days he ruled again, until Wellington and Blücher defeated him at Waterloo in 1815.

His soldiers called him "the little corporal", and British cartoons drew him tiny. In fact he was about 1.69 m tall, average or a little more for his time. French inches were longer than English ones, which added to the confusion.
pages.cap: A British cartoon of 1805: Pitt and a small Napoleon carve up the world

pages.x: The British sent him to St Helena, a remote island in the South Atlantic, 1,900 km from Africa. He spent his last years dictating his memoirs, and died there in 1821, aged 51.
Napoleon remade Europe. His wars killed millions, but his laws, schools and the idea that talent, not birth, should decide who rises spread across the continent.
pts: Crowned himself Emperor of the French
One of the greatest generals in history
